heroSummary: The Bambu Lab X1C handles eSUN PETG exceptionally well out of the box with its direct-drive extruder and hardened steel nozzle. By capping the maximum volumetric speed to 14 mm³/s, the system achieves reliable print speeds of up to 167 mm/s without risking underextrusion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with glue stick or liquid release agent to prevent permanent bonding
slicerTweaks: Set Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament settings to automatically cap linear flow at 167 mm/s for a 0.2mm layer height.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' (2mm wipe distance) and set 'Retract on layer change' to minimize PETG nozzle buildup and stringing.
Configure Part Cooling Fan to 0% for the first 3 layers, ramping between 20% min and 60% max, with the auxiliary chamber fan turned completely off (0%).
Set the Pressure Advance (PA) value between 0.032 and 0.038 using OrcaSlicer line calibration to prevent corner bulging at high acceleration.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe stringing and fine whisker buildup on travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and oozes readily due to residual moisture, combined with excessive print temperature or unoptimized wipe settings.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament in a dedicated dryer at 65°C for 6-8 hours, drop nozzle temp to 240°C, and enable a 2mm wipe on travel moves in OrcaSlicer.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Chunk of PEI coating torn off the build plate upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG exhibits excessive adhesion to smooth and semi-smooth PEI surfaces, causing molecular fusion when cooled.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a thin, even coat of liquid glue or PVA glue stick to serve as a sacrificial release agent, and let the bed cool fully to 30°C before flexing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Intermittent underextrusion or matte-streaked outer perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Exceeding the melt capacity of the hotend due to printing faster than the 14 mm³/s limit of eSUN PETG.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Enforce the 14 mm³/s Maximum Volumetric Speed clamp in the Filament Profile and decrease outer wall speed to 120 mm/s.

faq.question: Should I keep the X1C chamber door and top glass closed when printing eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: It is recommended to crack the front door or prop open the top lid slightly to keep chamber temperatures below 40°C, preventing heat creep in the direct drive extruder while eliminating draft-induced warping.

faq.question: Can I use the stock Bambu Generic PETG profile for eSUN PETG?
faq.answer: While the Generic PETG profile provides a baseline, it often runs the volumetric speed too high (up to 16 mm³/s) and the aux fan at 50%, causing layer adhesion loss; tuning volumetric flow to 14 mm³/s and disabling the aux fan yields significantly better results.

faq.question: Why is eSUN PETG leaving small charred blobs on my prints?
faq.answer: PETG naturally accumulates on the nozzle tip during direction changes and burns before depositing onto walls; enable nozzle wiping, use a clean silicone sock, and reduce flow ratio slightly if overextruding.

faq.question: What is the optimal bed temperature for eSUN PETG on the Bambu Textured PEI plate?
faq.answer: A target temperature of 75°C to 78°C provides optimal thermal bond without causing premature bottom-layer crystallization or foot warping.
